_readme: Felicis's live portfolio, straight from the site's own CMS. `site_stage` is the firm's own round label per company (Seed / Series A / Series B / Series C / Common) and `site_status` its own state enum (current | acquired | ipo); both are UNSCORED here and are measured against golden.json before the grind may treat them as labels. `description` states the entry round in words on the featured rows.
_source: Sanity project ggsokyyr, dataset production, public read API

rows.description: Felicis backed Adyen at Series A in 2014, when the company was still an under-the-radar Amsterdam payments startup, and doubled down later that year by joining its $250 million Series B as Adyen's growth accelerated.
rows.name: Adyen
rows.story_text: About Adyen Adyen is a global fintech platform that combines payments, data, and financial products into a single stack for enterprises. It lets businesses run payments and automated payouts, embed financial products like accounts, card issuing, and capital under their own brand, and manage everything through one API and centralized platform, all backed by US, UK, and EU banking licenses. Adyen serves major global brands like Adobe, Meta, Prada Group, and L'Occitane across retail, travel, digital media, and financial services.

rows.description: Felicis led Arena's Series A, after previously investing in the company's seed round.
rows.name: Arena
rows.story_text: About Arena Arena is the industry-standard, human-driven benchmark platform for evaluating AI models, turning millions of real-world user votes into the leaderboards that model labs and enterprises rely on to understand true model performance. Users submit a prompt, two anonymous model responses appear, and users vote for the stronger answer. Founded in 2025 by Anastasios Angelopoulos, Wei-Lin Chiang, and Ion Stoic the company grew out of a UC Berkeley research project (Chatbot Arena) into a platform used by over 5 million people across 150 countries each month, with labs like OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic relying on it for real-world evaluation data.

rows.description: Felicis first invested in Assort Health's $76 million Series B round in 2025, and later joined their $120 million Series C round in 2026.
rows.name: Assort Health
rows.story_text: Assort Health builds AI voice agents for healthcare providers, handling the entire patient journey — from scheduling and intake to triage, referrals, and follow-up. Its platform is trained on over 190 million patient interactions across 22+ specialties and integrates with more than 15 EHR and practice management systems. Providers using Assort have seen results like reduced hold times, higher patient conversion, and additional appointment revenue captured without adding headcount, and the agents have earned strong patient satisfaction ratings for handling everything from routine scheduling to complex care protocols.

rows.description: Felicis first invested in Canva in October 2015, leading a $15M Series A funding round.
rows.name: Canva
rows.story_text: About Canva Canva is an online design and publishing platform that lets anyone create visual content — from social posts and presentations to videos, websites, and print materials — without needing design expertise. Launched in 2013 with a mission to empower everyone in the world to design anything and publish anywhere, Canva has grown into a broad Visual Suite spanning documents, sheets, whiteboards, video editing, and a growing set of AI tools like Magic Write, Magic Layers, and an AI-powered code generator, along with brand management and enterprise features for teams. Companies like Zoom, Airbnb, Salesforce, and Bloomingdale's use Canva to power their content creation.

rows.description: Felicis backed Cruise as an early seed-stage investor, helping fund its initial $4.3 million capital raise before its historic acquisition by General Motors.
rows.name: Cruise
rows.story_text: About Cruise Cruise was a pioneer in autonomous vehicle technology, building self-driving systems aimed at bringing driverless robotaxi service to cities across the U.S. The company was an early leader in the space, operating driverless ride-hailing service in San Francisco and pushing the industry forward on what full autonomy could look like at scale. Cruise's technology and team were ultimately brought in-house at GM, where the work now informs the automaker's broader autonomous driving efforts, including its Super Cruise driver-assistance platform.

rows.description: Felicis backed DeepInfra from the very beginning, joining the company's seed round. Felicis co-led the $18 million Series A in 2025, and again participated in the $107 million Series B in 2026.
rows.name: DeepInfra
rows.story_text: About DeepInfra DeepInfra is building the inference layer AI companies run on — an AI inference cloud that lets developers deploy over 100 machine learning models spanning text, speech, image, video, and embeddings through simple, cost-effective APIs. The company runs its own inference-optimized infrastructure across secure US-based data centers, with a zero-retention policy and SOC 2 and ISO 27001 certification, giving customers a fast, secure alternative to building and managing GPU infrastructure themselves. For customers who want dedicated hardware, DeepInfra also offers DeepCluster, its own NVIDIA GPU clusters. Its founding team scaled the backend of imo, a messaging app with over 200 million monthly users, before turning that same expertise toward solving AI inference at scale. Customers include Hugging Face, and Salesforce.

rows.description: Felicis led Mercor's $100 million Series B in February 2025, and returned eight months later to lead its $350 million Series C.
rows.name: Mercor
rows.story_text: About Mercor Mercor is a marketplace and data platform that organizes human intelligence to power the AI economy, powering frontier research, RLHF data, and AI agent training at scale for top AI labs and enterprises. It connects domain experts — from doctors and engineers to consultants and scientists — with AI labs that need specialized human expertise to train and evaluate frontier models, spanning fields like medicine, law, engineering, and finance. Mercor also publishes APEX, a benchmark tracking AI productivity and capability across real-world professional tasks.

rows.description: Felicis was one of Notion's earliest backers, and has supported the company through its growth into a multibillion-dollar AI-native workspace.
rows.name: Notion
rows.story_text: About Notion Notion is the AI-native workspace that brings docs, knowledge bases, projects, and enterprise search into a single connected platform, with Custom Agents that automate repetitive work like triage, reporting, and Q&A around the clock. The company builds Custom Agents, enterprise search across all of a team's apps, and automation for busywork, all aimed at helping teams get more done, faster. Notion is used by millions of teams worldwide, including a large share of the Fortune 100 and YC companies, and is trusted by companies like OpenAI, Figma, Ramp, Cursor, and Vercel.

rows.description: Felicis was the very first seed check into Periodic Labs, helping the company get started on day one.
rows.name: Periodic Labs
rows.story_text: About Periodic Labs Periodic Labs is building AI scientists paired with autonomous physical laboratories, aiming to accelerate discovery in the physical sciences beyond what internet-scale text data alone can teach a model. The company is starting with the physical sciences, where experiments have high signal-to-noise, are relatively fast, and results are verifiable—with an early goal of discovering superconductors that work at higher temperatures than today's materials, which could have implications for transportation, power grids, space travel, and nuclear fusion. Its founding team includes people who co-created ChatGPT, DeepMind's GNoME, OpenAI's Operator (now Agent), the neural attention mechanism, and MatterGen, and who have scaled autonomous physics labs and contributed to major materials discoveries over the last decade.

rows.description: Felicis invested in Plaid's $12.5 million Series A funding round in 2014 and followed on in its $250 million Series C in 2018.
rows.name: Plaid
rows.story_text: About Plaid Plaid is a fintech infrastructure company that lets apps and services securely connect to people's bank accounts and financial data. Its network connects to over 12,000 financial institutions across 20 countries, powering more than one million daily connections and higher onboarding conversion for the companies built on it. Plaid's products span payments, fraud and risk prevention, identity verification, credit underwriting, and personal financial insights, giving developers the infrastructure to build things like bank payments, KYC/AML compliance, and budgeting tools without having to build bank connectivity themselves. Customers building on Plaid include Venmo, Carvana, and Robinhood.

rows.description: Felicis invested in Ring's $28 million Series B round in 2015 and followed on in their $61 million Series C round in 2016 and $109 million Series D round in 2017.
rows.name: Ring
rows.story_text: About Ring Ring makes smart home security products — video doorbells, indoor and outdoor cameras, alarms, and sensors — that let people monitor and protect their homes directly from their phone. Its Ring Protect Plans add features like extended video history, AI-generated video descriptions, facial recognition for tagging familiar faces, and 24/7 professional monitoring with emergency dispatch. Ring pioneered the connected video doorbell category and has been owned by Amazon since 2018.

rows.description: Felicis invested in Runlayer's $11 million seed in November 2025 and led the $30 million Series A in 2026.
rows.name: Runlayer
rows.story_text: About Runlayer Runlayer is an AI enablement and control platform that gives companies a governed way to roll out AI agents across their workforce while keeping security and IT in control. It offers a catalog of thousands of MCPs served through a governed gateway across major AI clients, lets teams turn internal APIs and workflows into reusable agent capabilities, and gives employees a way to create governed AI coworkers with scoped permissions. On the control side, Runlayer surfaces shadow AI from unmanaged agents and plugins, governs what users and agents can access, scans tool calls and outputs for risk in real time, and tracks AI spend and adoption across teams. Customers include Gusto, Jane, Cursor, PagerDuty, and dbt Labs.

rows.description: Felicis led Runway's $50 million Series C in December 2022, valuing the company at $500 million.
rows.name: Runway
rows.story_text: About Runway Runway is an AI research and product company building foundational General World Models capable of simulating all possible worlds and experiences, aiming to advance the next frontier of intelligence through models that can understand, perceive, generate, and act in the world. Its GWM-1 model comes in three variants — GWM Worlds for explorable environments, GWM Avatars for conversational characters, and GWM Robotics for robotic manipulation — alongside Gen-4.5, its state-of-the-art video generation model, and Characters, a real-time video agent API for building custom conversational personas. Runway partners with organizations across media, entertainment, and architecture, including Lionsgate, NVIDIA, and KPF, applying its models to filmmaking, robotics, and creative workflows.

rows.description: Felicis first invested in Shopify in December 2010 as part of the company's $7 million Series A round.
rows.name: Shopify
rows.story_text: About Shopify Shopify is an all-in-one commerce platform that lets businesses build online stores, sell in person, and reach customers across social and AI channels from a single system. It includes a website builder, point-of-sale, order and inventory management, shipping, marketing and analytics tools, and a checkout with Shop Pay that converts significantly higher than standard guest checkout. Sidekick, its built-in commerce AI assistant, helps merchants spot growth opportunities and automate tedious tasks, while a broad ecosystem of apps lets businesses extend the platform for virtually any specialized need. Shopify serves merchants at every stage, from solo entrepreneurs to global enterprises.

rows.description: Felicis first led Supabase's $80 million Series B in May 2022 and has participated in every round since, including the Series D in April 2025 and the $500 million Series F in June 2026.
rows.name: Supabase
rows.story_text: About Supabase Supabase is an open-source backend platform built on Postgres, positioned as an alternative to Firebase for building web and mobile applications. It bundles a dedicated Postgres database with auto-generated REST and GraphQL APIs, built-in authentication with social logins and row-level security, S3-compatible object storage with a global CDN, globally distributed edge functions, real-time sync over WebSockets, and a vector toolkit for AI embeddings — all working together out of the box. The platform is fully open source and self-hostable, built on Postgres to avoid vendor lock-in, SOC2 Type 2 compliant, and available across 16+ global regions.

rows.description: Felicis invested in Twitch's 2007 $8 million seed round (as Justin.tv) and followed on in its September 2012 $15 million Series B round.
rows.name: Twitch
rows.story_text: About Twitch Twitch is an interactive livestreaming service for content spanning gaming, entertainment, sports, music, and more. It lets creators broadcast live to audiences in real time, with viewers able to chat, react, and support streamers directly, and it has become the dominant platform for live gaming content as well as a hub for esports, music, talk shows, and "IRL" streaming. Twitch has been owned by Amazon since 2014.

rows.description: Felicis led n8n's $12 million Series A in 2021 and followed on in its $60 million Series B and $180M Series C in 2025.
rows.name: n8n
rows.story_text: About n8n n8n is a workflow automation platform that uniquely combines AI capabilities with business process automation, giving technical teams the flexibility of code with the speed of no-code. It offers a broad library of integrations, lets users build AI agents with multi-agent setups and RAG systems while keeping every step traceable and inspectable, and can be deployed on-prem or in the cloud for teams that want full control over their data. n8n is open source with a large and active community, and is used by companies like Microsoft, Meta, NVIDIA, and Vodafone to automate everything from IT operations to security workflows.
